title: Euglycemic DKA with an SGLT2 Inhibitor
question: What is the most likely diagnosis and next step?
clinicalScenario: A 54-year-old patient with type 2 diabetes takes empagliflozin and basal insulin. After 2 days of vomiting and markedly reduced oral intake, the patient reports abdominal pain, nausea, and rapid breathing.

choices.label: A
choices.text: DKA is unlikely because the glucose is below 250 mg/dL

choices.label: B
choices.text: Euglycemic DKA; arrange urgent emergency evaluation and hold the SGLT2 inhibitor

choices.label: C
choices.text: Hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state; encourage oral hydration at home

choices.label: D
choices.text: Simple viral gastroenteritis; continue all diabetes medications

explanation: The patient has high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and significant ketosis despite a glucose of only 178 mg/dL.
SGLT2 inhibitors such as empagliflozin can cause euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis. Important findings include an elevated anion gap, low bicarbonate, acidemia, and elevated beta-hydroxybutyrate.
The relatively normal glucose does not exclude DKA. Vomiting and reduced oral intake can precipitate euglycemic DKA in a patient taking an SGLT2 inhibitor.
clinicalPearl: Consider euglycemic DKA in patients taking an SGLT2 inhibitor who develop nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, or tachypnea even when glucose is below 250 mg/dL. Urgent emergency evaluation is appropriate.

title: ACE Inhibitor Creatinine Increase in Diabetic CKD
question: What is the most appropriate next step?
clinicalScenario: A 58-year-old patient with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents for follow-up.
Medications: metformin and amlodipine 10 mg daily.
Initial findings: BP 148/88 mmHg, creatinine 1.0 mg/dL, potassium 4.3 mEq/L, eGFR 78 mL/min/1.73 m², and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 420 mg/g.
Because of persistent hypertension and significant albuminuria, lisinopril is started.
Two weeks later: BP 136/80 mmHg, creatinine 1.25 mg/dL, potassium 4.8 mEq/L, and the patient feels well.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Stop lisinopril immediately because creatinine increased

choices.label: B
choices.text: Continue lisinopril and monitor renal function and potassium

choices.label: D
choices.text: Refer the patient urgently to the emergency department
